newsitem.title: USA: CMS Energy close to sealing India power plant deal.
newsitem.headline: CMS Energy close to sealing India power plant deal.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp officials said Wednesday that they hoped to secure counterguarantees from the Indian government this month for a 250 megawatt power plant project in Tamil Nadu, India.
The company has been waiting for more than a year for the counterguarantees in order to seal financing for the coal-fired power plant in Neyveli.

"Our hope is that we can get this counterguarantee done by the end of the month," said CMS Energy president Victor Fryling, adding that he hoped that the fact that India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is from Tamil Nadu would help.
"We actually have a draft of it in our hands. So there is progress -- it's the first time we've had a draft," Fryling said at a press briefing.
"It needs some minor negotiations I think to complete it," including getting the Tamil Nadu government to sign off on the project for the third or fourth time, he said.
Company officials said while they were still interested in expanding in India, they had cut back their activities there because the government approval process was too slow.

CMS Energy is already involved in a project to double the size of a 235 megawatt GVK Industries power plant in Andhra Pradesh, and is considering building an LNG gasification terminal and 1200 megawatts of power generation, and looking at coal projects in India.

"We're kind of in a 'show me' attitude, where we're asking the government: 'Show me that this is a good place to make an investment, and we'll do a lot here," Fryling said, adding, "And we're still waiting for the results."
"If the government can speed its process up, we certainly can be there to make the investments as they're needed," said CMS Energy chairman William McCormick.
